name: Daniel Monteavaro (moncho1929)
statement:
My artistic practice explores the dynamic intersection between civic memory, human resilience, and vibrant public architecture. Over the past twenty years, I have developed a visual language that synthesizes bold contemporary figurative storytelling, rhythmic urban line work, and radiant color harmony. I treat color not merely as decorative surface treatment, but as an active emotional architecture—employing saturated mineral tones, warm gradations, and intentional negative space to engage passersby across a bustling market hall while offering intimate, evocative narrative details upon closer viewing. My public works celebrate community identity by honoring historical foundations while visually expressing contemporary growth, vitality, and cultural fellowship.

Technically, my practice is grounded in my early classical apprenticeship in stone conservation and architectural restoration at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in New York (1994–1996). This background instilled an uncompromising structural rigor in my approach to surfaces, environmental longevity, and material permanence. Across my career, I have successfully executed monumental civic installations nationwide, ranging from multi-story facades to 60,000-square-foot sports plaza activations. Recent representative civic projects include the City of Los Angeles Department of Cultural Affairs Homeless Navigation Center Mural (2023; $35,000; 50 × 15 ft masonry mural) and the City of West Hollywood City Hall Facade Mural (2024; $25,000; 40 × 20 ft exterior concrete facade). I am fully certified in aerial boom and scissor lift operations, hold comprehensive commercial general liability insurance ($2,000,000 aggregate / $1,000,000 per occurrence), and possess extensive experience managing clean, quiet, and dust-controlled installations in active public gathering spaces.

Developing a signature indoor mural for NewBo City Market represents a compelling civic opportunity that holds profound regional resonance for my studio: my original paintings are already held in the permanent collection of The Figge Art Museum in Davenport, Iowa (~70 miles from Cedar Rapids). This gives me an enduring institutional commitment to eastern Iowa's cultural community. I approach this project with deep respect for NewBo City Market's role as a vibrant culinary and artisan incubator, a community event center, and a living symbol of urban resilience. I look forward to collaborating closely with Murals & More, the selection committee, and district stakeholders to design an iconic, welcoming visual anchor that honors Cedar Rapids' rich heritage and inspires visitors for years to come.
